Subject: Velocity metrics bridge: OKR checkpoint & QBR artifacts

Folks,

I pulled together the November KPI dashboard and a short bridge for the leadership QBR. High-level signals you should be aware of (see attachments and linked folder):

- Latency: 95th P90 for text-gen spiked from 280ms -> 560ms overnight (window: 02:00-03:30 PST). Initial traces point to a change in request size distribution and one serving cluster with degraded batching efficiency.
- Cost: ~12% month-over-month increase in per-token cost on the quantized Llama-variants; most visible on long-context workloads from a few enterprise accounts.
- Uptime: brief 0.28% dip in us-west (00:45–01:05) tied to rolling node maintenance; customer impact limited but noteworthy for QBR.
- Usage: steady growth in embedding calls (+22% MoM) concentrated in scheduled batch jobs (03:00 UTC window).

As prep for the QBR and our OKR checkpoint I need the following by EOD Wednesday (ask owners below):

1) Root-cause owners & brief corrective plan for each signal (1–2 lines). Owner: Markus for latency, Soojin for cost economics, Irene for uptime, Laura for usage/customer outreach.
2) Decision on a conservative canary for the new batching kernel (proposed: 5% traffic, auto-fallback). If approved, Ops needs a go/no-go and rollout window.
3) One-slide summary suitable for execs (title + 3 bullets) by Thursday morning for the QBR pack. Laura, I'll take the exec narrative if you can send the slide by Thu 09:00 PST.

Attachments: nov-dashboard-screenshots.pdf, qbr-okr-matrix-2026.xlsx (also in Drive).

I'll coordinate a short 30-min triage if helpful; propose Wed 10:30 PST. Please reply inline with owners' confirmations.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher

Thanks for the succinct bridge, Sean. I'm taking the owner lane on latency. Quick notes:

- I can confirm the spike correlates with a spike in median request length from two enterprise customers (FastApp and one internal load test). Batching efficiency dropped due to fewer coalesced short requests.
- Immediate plan: roll a temporary routing tweak to prefer coalescing short requests in the affected cluster and increase batching window from 10ms -> 25ms for a 2-hour window tonight (low-risk). That should bring P95 down ~30% based on simulations.

I agree a 30-min dive is warranted. I'm available Wed 10:30 PST.

On Mon, Nov 16, 2026 at 10:05 AM Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com> wrote:

Thanks for the heads-up. Quick update from platform: the 00:45–01:05 us-west uptime blip was caused by an automated node OS patch that coincided with a scaledown event; the control plane failed to reschedule one StatefulSet quickly due to a transient API timeout.

Action taken: we disabled the aggressive auto-patch window for the affected pool, rescheduled the StatefulSet, and added a retry layer to the rescheduler. Monitoring alert thresholds adjusted to reduce noise.

Recommendation: we should still avoid a broad canary until Markus's batching tweak is verified in prod—small canaries OK but skip heavy traffic routes.

Irene
VP, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
